A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GIFT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Their experiments and supplementary material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original explanation-generation, intervention, and ablation results on CLEVR, CelebA, and BDD-OIA, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical experiments and reports additional causal measurements. Its separately cited human-study results are attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Stage 4 now uses signed CaCE and class-specific PNS, with PNS guiding CelebA ranking and refinement, instead of absolute-CaCE-only verification. Counterfactual generation, captioning, and LLM aggregation remain unchanged. V1's Stage 5 survives as further exploration in v2 Section 3.5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CLEVR classification rules and supporting datasets, CelebA age classification, and deliberately biased BDD-OIA turn-right classifier. No additional domain, task, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 consolidates the independent-caption, LLM-only, and attributed human/counterfactual comparisons already discussed in v1 Section 4.4 and Appendix F. Additional example citations do not document newly evaluated baseline implementations.

E3.justification: V2 adds PNS to causal evaluation, replaces operative absolute CaCE with signed CaCE, and selects CelebA concept combinations using PNS ≥ 5%. These revise scoring and selection within retained experiments. The documented classifiers, training budgets, splits, and verification sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Section 4.1 adds an analysis of CaCE–PNS agreement for true and overspecified CLEVR rules, while CelebA combination exploration drops the gray-hair/eye-wrinkle case. Existing captioning ablations, counterfactual-count sensitivity analyses, and the ResNet failure analysis remain, often relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. V2's PNS scores add a causal-effect metric rather than uncertainty estimates; the intervention sampling and empirical aggregation approach remain.

E6.justification: V2 adds PNS measurements across all three use cases; BDD gains 53/47/29% alongside unchanged CaCE 51/45/27%. CelebA CaCE revisions include receding hairline 6.5→2.0% and glasses 10.5→11.5%, while gray-hair causal and combination results disappear. CLEVR success remains 11/12. These are added or revised measurements, not demonstrated performance gains; the CelebA revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A.2 only mentions necessary-and-sufficient causality as an alternative. V2 Appendices A.2–A.3 develop PN, PS, and PNS definitions and estimators, state an intervention-based lower bound, and prove CaCE = PNS1 − PNS0. V2 also adopts signed rather than absolute CaCE as its operative definition.

C1.justification: V2 adds an explicit contribution claiming analysis of two complementary causal metrics and their relationship. The central contribution—global, interpretable, faithful textual explanations derived from counterfactuals—and the three demonstrated application claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets metric agreement through causal directionality and discusses CelebA findings using class-specific PNS. Appendix G adds computational-cost limitations and a suggestion to encourage hypothesis recall through prompting. Existing limitations concerning counterfactual scope, caption noise, image editing, and unsuccessful automated refinement remain.

D1.justification: V2 specifies DI ≥ 15% and PNS ≥ 5% selection thresholds; component models, prompts, and detailed training information are retained. Release wording becomes inconsistent: the abstract says the framework is released, while the new Impact Statement promises future code/data release, whereas v1 explicitly states code, data, and models are released.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including OpenBias, Tian and Pearl's causation work, Radford et al., and Singla et al., while removing citations such as Flamingo, Mistral, and Gemma. The main explanation-method taxonomy and counterfactual-grounded positioning remain, with more explicit method-family comparisons.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction, condenses related work, revises the conclusion, and reorganizes the narrative around four stages plus further exploration. V1 Section 4.4 is redistributed across the BDD discussion and appendices. The supplementary contents page is removed and an Impact Statement added.

P2.justification: V1's introductory use-case figure is removed, and its pipeline diagram is substantially redrawn as v2 Figure 1. V2 adds method-family and comparison tables, expands result displays with PNS columns, relocates appendix tables and figures, and adopts a different page layout and caption style.

improvement.justification: The PNS derivation and paired causal scores make verification more informative, while the revised overview clarifies manual refinement. These provide a limited net gain in analytical clarity. Benefits are tempered by unexplained CelebA score revisions and new inconsistencies: Figure 4 states DI ≥ 15% despite displaying evaluated concepts below that threshold, and Appendix A.3's reverse-direction statement omits a minus sign.
